source.title: Meta-LR-Schedule-Net: Learned LR Schedules that Scale and Generalize
source.authors: Jun Shu; Yanwen Zhu; Qian Zhao; De-Yu Meng; Zong-Ben Xu

record.file_problem: The supplied text is a full paper; no material truncation or garbling is apparent.
record.tranche_reason: Compares Adam with SGD-based methods and reports held-out performance, using this paper’s LR-schedule experiments rather than the optimizer comparisons in V4’s cited studies.
record.gate_note: The paper reports optimizer comparisons relevant to V4. LR schedule transfer, corrupted-data robustness, and the other experiments do not test the listed claim versions. Figure values without textual numerical descriptions are not extracted as rows.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own Adam-versus-SGD and momentum-SGD held-out comparisons on image classification and word-level language modeling. These test V4 despite appearing as baselines in an LR-schedule paper; the study is not an original source.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the authors' conclusion: MLR-SNet learns adaptive LR schedules that transfer across heterogeneous tasks with competitive performance and robustness. The authors report that default Adam underperforms strong image-task schedules and suggest extra tuning. Table 3 independently shows Adam outperforming SGD on Penn Treebank; the accompanying prose primarily compares MLR-SNet with both optimizers.
record.recipe_differences: The paper compares Adam and SGD-based LR schedules in experiments on CIFAR and Penn Treebank; it does not reproduce the optimizer-comparison methods or tuning protocols named in V4.
record.method_sensitivity: The direction of the Adam versus SGD+Val Strategy comparison differs between the image results and Penn Treebank results; the paper also uses different LR schedules and task-specific settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 5.3 visualizes train and test losses along Gaussian random rays from solutions and describes competitive methods as occupying flat regions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Some competitive LR schedules yield solutions with broad low-loss regions along sampled directions; this does not establish V7's magnitude-aware sharpness–generalization-gap ranking.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
record.problems: Only three seeds are reported for experiments. The image comparison uses Adam’s default settings while SGD schedule baselines use specified settings; no equal-training-performance comparison is reported. The text does not give exact numerical values for the plotted image and language results outside the tables.
record.rows_left_out: No additional numerical optimizer-comparison rows were omitted. Figures 3, 4, 7–9, and 13 contain plotted comparisons, but the supplied text does not state exact values for those curves.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting alongside natural-label and random-label held-out accuracy.
Classifier width beyond interpolation and its effect on test error; varying the LR meta-learner's width does not test this.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
A controlled optimizer tuning-budget comparison; broader hyperparameter searches; decoupled weight decay; switching from Adam to SGD; and established equal or better Adam training performance.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove a large-batch penalty.
Controlled addition or removal of dropout and weight decay.
Magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance, measured generalization gaps, and ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized training examples versus matched random removals.

missing.what: Momentum-SGD comparisons, especially schedule dependence: CIFAR-10 fixed LR 87.69 ± 0.14 versus Adam 90.86 ± 0.15; MultiStep 95.08 ± 0.13 versus Adam 90.86 ± 0.15. CIFAR-100 MultiStep 80.74 ± 0.19 versus Adam 68.94 ± 0.24. Record the remaining conventional schedules as well to preserve the comparison's scope.

Final-epoch clean accuracy after training on corrupted images: across 15 corruptions, Adam versus MultiStep is 80.29 ± 1.64 versus 85.36 ± 1.71 on CIFAR-10 and 43.76 ± 2.22 versus 52.16 ± 2.59 on CIFAR-100. Across 14 non-Gaussian corruptions, corresponding values are 80.39 ± 1.65 versus 85.48 ± 1.71 and 43.94 ± 2.18 versus 52.28 ± 2.44. These are direct optimizer comparisons, not merely MLR-SNet robustness results. Uncertainty summarizes variation across corruption models.

record.verdict_notes: V4 already includes Adam doing better on word-level language models, so R3–R4 warrant support for that clause rather than challenges. The study does not establish a matched tuning protocol or an intrinsic optimizer disadvantage. Best-epoch values in Tables 5–6 are selected performance summaries and should remain distinguished from final-epoch results. Additional plotted optimizer comparisons are already declared in rows_left_out; no exact curve values are inferred.

versions.untested_parts: Memorization of random labels and generalization on natural labels.
Width sweeps beyond interpolation and test error.
Broader tuning; decoupled weight decay; switching from Adam to SGD; word-level language models where Adam does better; equal or better training-performance comparisons.
Large versus small batches under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with the train-test gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting test accuracy.

rows.subject: ResNet-18 on CIFAR-10
rows.operation_detail: Trained with Adam using the paper’s default parameter setting; test accuracy compared with SGD+MultiStep.
rows.note: Adam’s reported test accuracy is lower than SGD+MultiStep; the study does not establish equal or better training performance for Adam.
rows.check: The numbers are correct. Adam trails SGD+MultiStep by 2.96 percentage points, clearly exhibiting V4's image-task effect. Equal or better training performance is an optional qualifier, not required for this result. Adam uses defaults rather than a documented learning-rate search.

rows.subject: WideResNet-28-10 on CIFAR-100
rows.operation_detail: Trained with Adam using the paper’s default parameter setting; test accuracy compared with SGD+MultiStep.
rows.note: Adam’s reported test accuracy is lower than SGD+MultiStep; the study does not establish equal or better training performance for Adam.
rows.check: The numbers are correct. Adam trails SGD+MultiStep by 8.10 percentage points, clearly exhibiting V4's image-task effect. Missing training-performance comparisons do not make this effect partial.

rows.subject: 2-layer LSTM on Penn Treebank
rows.operation_detail: Trained with Adam+Val Strategy; compared with SGD+Val Strategy.
rows.note: Lower perplexity indicates better held-out performance; Adam+Val Strategy is better than SGD+Val Strategy in this setting.
rows.check: The numbers are correct. Adam's lower perplexity exhibits V4's explicit word-level-language-model exception, so it does not reverse or challenge the full version. Specify Adam's initial LR 0.01, gradient moving-average weight 0, and validation-triggered decay.

rows.subject: 3-layer LSTM on Penn Treebank
rows.operation_detail: Trained with Adam+Val Strategy; compared with SGD+Val Strategy.
rows.note: Lower perplexity indicates better held-out performance; Adam+Val Strategy is better than SGD+Val Strategy in this setting.
rows.check: The numbers are correct. Adam's lower perplexity agrees with V4's explicit word-level-language-model exception. The reported means favor Adam; no significance test is supplied. Include the same Adam settings as R3.
